source_snapshot.items: Test BMC I2C-10 connectivity to the HMC IO expander and both carrier-board IO expanders
source_snapshot.procedure: On BMC run `i2cdetect -y -q 9`, then forced reads of address0x74 registers0x01 and0x00; consult PID1114953.
source_snapshot.criteria: Only generic evidence/photo and unexpected-log checks; no three-instance selection, register definition, pin mapping or expected masks.
source_snapshot.deepseek: NO; invents probing/soldering instead of evaluating the remote register reads.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: MANUAL ONLY/CHANGED; recognizes that one address cannot prove three paths and flags `-f`, but still requires unsourced physical inspection and does not distinguish expander instances from two ports of one device.
source_snapshot.items_direct_xlsx: Test connections between BMC I2C-10 and IO expander on HMC and both IO expanders on both carrier boards
source_snapshot.procedure_direct_xlsx: "【Before Test】 1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition. 2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.). Log into the BMC and run the following command and ensure you get a reply. Refer to PID : 1114953 for other devices expected on the bus. i2cdetect -y -q 9 i2ctransfer -f -y 9 w1@0x74 0x01 r1; i2ctransfer -f -y 9 w1@0x74 0x00 r1
source_snapshot.criteria_direct_xlsx: 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test."
source_snapshot.deepseek_direct_xlsx: NO | -- not runnable by agent: testing the physical I2C connection/link between the named components (BMC I2C-10 and IO expander on HMC and both IO expanders on both carrier boards) is a hardware-integrity check that requires probing/soldering the actual I2C traces and collecting photos per the criteria; the agent cannot touch the hardware or take photos over SSH.

test_case.test_name: Test connections between BMC I2C-10 and IO expander on HMC and both IO expanders on both carrier boards — retained controlled review-layer procedure
test_case.purpose: Verify BMC I2C-10 reaches the IO expander on HMC and the separate IO expanders on both carrier boards, with correct read-only port state for every named instance and no GPIO changes.
required_package: PID1114953 mapping from BMC I2C-10 to bus9 and HMC/carrier-A/carrier-B expander instances
Per-instance upstream mux/segment selection and address, especially any repeated0x74 alias
Expander part/revision and definitions for registers0x00/0x01, including input/output/config semantics
Expected pin name, polarity, direction and input/status mask for each instance
Kernel/daemon GPIO expander bindings and owner-approved driver interface or force exception
Timeout/NACK/error criteria, unchanged output/direction verification and recovery
test_case.test_command: Map BMC I2C-10 to bus9 and enumerate the three expander instances/selection paths from PID1114953; identify address and part per instance; inspect driver ownership and direction/output state; read only the approved input/status registers (including0x00/0x01 where applicable); compare pin masks against platform presence/strap state; repeat independently for HMC, carrier A and carrier B; verify directions/outputs remain unchanged.
test_case.expected_result: 【After Test】 1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders. 2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test."

Define whether0x74 registers0x00/0x01 are input ports, expected pin/polarity/direction/value masks for each instance, driver ownership and whether `-f` is allowed, safe scan policy, no-GPIO-change verification, timeouts and recovery. Confirm physical probing is not mandatory unless separately scoped.
safety_gate: Do not equate two register offsets with two or three devices
Do not run broad quick-write discovery on bus9
Prefer GPIO/driver read interfaces and avoid `-f` on a bound expander unless explicitly approved
Confirm0x00/0x01 are read-safe for the exact part; never write direction/output registers
Capture and compare direction/output state; abort on any GPIO transition, device ambiguity, NACK, timeout, stuck bus or management regression
expected_evidence: PID topology for BMC I2C-10/bus9 to HMC, carrier-A and carrier-B expanders
Register and pin/polarity/direction/value oracle for each expander
Timestamped read transcript and expected-versus-observed masks per instance
Pre/post configuration/output/input state showing no unintended GPIO change
BMC/bus/consumer health and engineer verdict for all three instances
test_case.recovery: Wistron I2C policy requires controller/bus, every target instance/address and expected response. GPIO expander ownership and output preservation are mandatory because these pins may control platform hardware.

source_conflict.reason: The source names three expanders but provides two offsets at one address with no routing or pin oracle; those offsets may belong to one device. It also omits driver ownership and earlier reviews invent physical probing.

blocked.reason: A safe review-layer method is defined; missing project values are runtime gates rather than a review blocker.
